capabilities: Track any folder (or the vault root) as its own Git repository
Stage, commit, discard and diff changes from a Source Control panel
Create, switch, merge and delete branches, and stash changes
Push, pull, sync and fetch, with per-repository auto-commit and auto-push schedules
Browse commit history and restore files to earlier versions
extras: Desktop only (mobile is unsupported). Access tokens are stored unencrypted in the plugin's data.json, and the README devotes a detailed privacy section to this risk, including a migration note about a plaintext credential file in versions up to 1.0.4. The manifest notes the plugin has not been reviewed by Obsidian staff.
intentEvidence: Unlike plugins that treat the whole vault as a single repository, Folder Git lets you manage multiple independent Git repositories, one per folder.
problem: Obsidian Git plugins treat the whole vault as a single repository, so users who want separate repositories per folder have no way to manage them inside Obsidian.

relations.evidence: It works with GitHub and Forgejo / Gitea (including Codeberg and self-hosted instances).
Create a new remote repository while adding a folder: under your account or one of your organizations, private or public.

requires.name: Git installed on the system or a configured Git binary path
GitHub personal access token or Forgejo/Gitea access token

summary: Git source control that manages an independent Git repository for each folder, with staging, commits, branches, push/pull, history and GitHub or Forgejo remotes.
